sector: Alternative asset management (real assets, private credit)
brlm: Axis Capital; Jefferies India; Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors; Nuvama Wealth Management

anchor.source: Anchor portion 21,62,161 shares (about Rs 360 cr at Rs 1,665), bid 23-Oct-2026; allocation report on nsearchives.nseindia.com not reachable

reference_note: Upper band Rs 1,665 (NSE issue page). At Rs 1,665: market cap Rs 10,702.7 cr (Rs 10,815.1 cr fully diluted); P/E 41.3x FY26 diluted EPS (40.8x on diluted shares, 33.5x on annualised Q1 FY27); P/B 9.3x Jun-26 diluted book. Pure OFS: no new money for the company.

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -62.3% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
model.reverse_dcf: The price asks the business to deliver 58.9 times its current free cash flow, in perpetuity.

call_basis: Call rule (ROUTINE.md hard rule 6), judged at the Rs 1,665 upper band: Neutral value Rs 1,130 is 32.1% below and Bull value Rs 1,214 is 27.1% below, so the Avoid limb applies on valuation, narrowly. At the Rs 1,585 floor the Neutral gap is 28.7%, which would read Neutral; the rule turns Neutral at or below about Rs 1,615. No material issue was found.
headline: A scaled alternatives manager (fee-paying AUM Rs 48,623 cr, +27% a year) priced at 41x FY26 earnings, in line with listed asset managers (median 38.7x); our fair value is Rs 1,130 (Neutral) because the DCF does not support peer multiples and profit benefits from capitalised distribution costs. Avoid at Rs 1,665, narrowly; it would be Neutral at about Rs 1,615 or below.
red_flags: Revenue from operations Rs 492.58 cr -> Rs 869.54 cr FY24-26 (+33% a year); Q1 FY27 +44%; fee-paying AUM Rs 48,623 cr at Jun-26 (Add. pp. 7, 107)
Carry (Variable Additional Return) Rs 290.47 cr = 33% of FY26 revenue, booked at fair value; realised carry Rs 430.69 cr in FY26 and Rs 338.10 cr in Q1 FY27 (Add. pp. 7, 108)
Distribution costs capitalised: prepaid balance Rs 667.94 cr at Jun-26; expensing the FY26 increase would cut pre-tax profit by Rs 167.03 cr - adjusted P/E 73.6x vs 40.8x reported (part 5)
Pure OFS of Rs 1,200 cr by Edelweiss Securities and Investments; Rs 205.70 cr dividend paid to the group in FY26; MD & CEO resigned Sep-2025 (DRHP p. 272; Add. p. 108)
At Rs 1,665: P/E 40.8x on diluted shares (peer median 38.7x), P/B 9.3x; fair value Rs 1,033 / 1,130 / 1,214 (Bear / Neutral / Bull)

strengths: One of India's larger alternatives platforms: AUM Rs 65,504 cr (Sep-25), fee-paying AUM Rs 48,623 cr (Jun-26) (DRHP p. 222; Add. p. 7)
Funds in third and fourth series; 73% of AUM from repeat clients (DRHP p. 222)
ROE 25.97% in FY26 with modest capex (Add. p. 7)
Management fees up 20-21% a year FY25-26 (Add. p. 7)
Asset operating platform (Sekura) for infrastructure portfolios (DRHP p. 222)
weaknesses: Carry is a third of revenue and lumpy; FY23 PAT (Rs 322.19 cr) was higher than FY25 (DRHP p. 19)
Capitalised distribution costs flatter reported profit while fund-raising grows (Add. p. 119)
Cost-to-income 63.8% (FY26), 68.5% in Q1 FY27, well above AMC peers (Add. p. 7)
MD & CEO resigned in Sep-2025; now led by two CEOs (DRHP p. 272)
Group linkages: brand, past rights purchases, dividend to promoter (DRHP pp. 22-24)
opportunities: Indian alternatives industry growth (issuer-paid CARE report, DRHP p. 158)
Infrastructure yield, InvIT and energy-transition funds (DRHP p. 223)
Global and GIFT City fund-raising (DRHP p. 223)
Realisation of accrued carry in maturing funds (Add. p. 108)
threats: Fund underperformance reducing carry and fund-raising (DRHP p. 20)
Valuation subjectivity in unlisted fund assets (DRHP p. 20)
Tax and regulatory changes for AIFs (DRHP p. 20)
Overhang: promoter group holds about 84% after the OFS
